1. THE SCENE — inside the Kazakh yurt from <<<image_1>>>, an evening after sunset, years after the loss. THE ELDER (Aksakal) from <<<image_2>>> speaks to ANA from <<<image_3>>>, the mother who has searched for her lost daughter for years and will not stop. He tells her plainly that so much time has passed, that the wolves have cost the people many lives, that it is time for her to stop. ANA does not answer. She sits holding and slowly turning her lost daughter's small wooden toy in her hands. Her silence and her hands are her refusal. The scene ends on that refusal, wordless and unshakable.
2. FRAME-BY-FRAME HAND-DRAWN FEEL — every frame looks painted by hand, a gentle constant boil in the painted lines and brushstrokes, texture and contours subtly redrawn each frame, never frozen, never mechanically smooth, never interpolated or morphed. The hand of the animator visible in every frame, across the whole scene.
3. LENS AND FOCAL LENGTH — anamorphic cinema lenses, shot like real film. Each shot has its own focal length: the wide two-shot on a ~35mm for natural perspective holding both figures and the room; the coverage on the Elder on a ~50mm normal lens for an honest undistorted portrait; the insert of the hands on a ~85mm with a shallow focus so the background falls soft; the close on Ana on a ~85mm portrait lens for gentle compression and intimacy. Keep any shallow depth of field SOFT and SUBTLE, a gentle painterly fall-off of the background, never a strong photographic bokeh blur that would break the hand-drawn look.
4. LIGHT AND EXPOSURE — evening after sunset, a LOW-KEY DIM interior, overall noticeably DARKER and dimmer than daylight, deep rich shadows filling much of the frame, a moody dark dusk atmosphere — but NOT crushed to flat black, the characters' faces still clearly visible and readable within the gloom. Find the balance: dark, low-key and atmospheric, yet faces legible. The only light is the last weak afterglow of dusk seeping softly down through the round shanyrak opening above — VERY SOFT, diffuse, dim, NOT directional. ABSOLUTELY NO visible light rays, NO shafts, NO beams, NO god rays, NO hard streaks, NO volumetric light — cheap AI slop. The dim dusk light fades in softly from above with soft feathered edges, no hard line, giving just enough gentle fill to keep faces and features readable while everything stays dim and shadowy. Richer shadows, lower exposure, but faces never lost. No warm glow, no bounce from carpet, no fire, no lamp.
5. WHITE BALANCE AND COLOR — correct natural white balance, neutral and true, NOT a heavy blue color cast, NOT an electric-blue night filter, only very slightly cool as natural dusk but neutral overall. White and pale things believable near-white — ANA's head cloth soft off-white, the ELDER's beard natural grey-white, felt neutral. Muted, desaturated, warm earthy darkness, deep and dim, true neutral balance, like a properly graded low-key film night interior, never the fake uniform blue tint of AI footage.
6. THE ELDER'S CHARACTER — a wise, firm, dignified elder. He does NOT whine, plead, or beg for pity, NOT weepy or self-pitying. He speaks the truth as it is — calm, steady, grounded, with the quiet authority of an old man who has earned the right to say a hard thing. Bitterness and the weight of years, but no weakness, no tears, no trembling. Plainly: enough, accept it. Strength and hard-earned wisdom, not sorrow.
7. ACTING IS EVERYTHING — long heavy silences between his phrases, restraint, no big gestures. Emotion reads through the visible faces, the eyes, posture, the angle and weight of the head, shoulders, hands, breath and stillness, drawn on twos as held painted poses. Give the pauses real time.
8. THE ELDER'S PERFORMANCE AND FACIAL MICRO-ACTING — he sits upright and composed in profile, head level, dignified, his lined face dim but clearly visible, speaking slowly and evenly. His face is alive with restrained micro-expression drawn on twos as held poses: slow heavy blinks of tired old eyes; his grey brows moving with weight — drawing together in a faint grave furrow on the hard words, lifting just slightly in weariness in the pauses; the deep lines of his brow and around his eyes shifting; small movements of the mouth and jaw beneath the beard as he forms words and presses his lips between phrases; the faint tightening of the eyes of a man carrying old sorrow. All of it grave, controlled, dignified — the micro-acting of calm authority, never twitchy, never weepy, never pleading. His steady gaze and upright bearing carry his strength.
9. ANA'S PERFORMANCE AND FACIAL MICRO-ACTING — she sits folded down over her hands, head bowed low, her worn grief-hollowed face dim and shadowed under her head cloth but STILL VISIBLE and readable, never a black void — her lowered eyes, features and quiet grief seen. Restrained micro-expression on twos: a faint tightening of the jaw, slow heavy blinks, the brows drawing faintly together, eyes glistening but never spilling, breath catching once. Her hands slowly turn the little wooden toy, her thumb stroking its worn surface. At his hardest words her hands still and close around it. She never speaks.
10. THE WOODEN TOY — her lost daughter's keepsake: a small simple hand-carved wooden toy, a little carved animal figure, worn smooth and darkened from years of being held, a humble child's plaything the mother made or kept. Small, precious, the only thing of her daughter she has left. She cradles and turns it in her hands, her thumb running over the smooth worn wood.
11. SECONDARY ACTION ON EVERYTHING THAT MOVES — follow-through and overlapping action drawn on twos: THE ELDER's beard and the cuffs skirts and trim of his chapan shift and settle with delayed motion as he breathes and speaks; ANA's head cloth and kimeshek ends and chapan folds stir softly with her breath and small movements, loose hair drifts; both their breath-vapor curls faintly in the cold dim air on twos; dust floats softly. Nothing rigid — every motion has secondary follow-through and overlap, alive and hand-drawn.
12. THE TOY IS THE HEART — ANA's hands slowly, continuously turn and cradle her daughter's small carved wooden toy, her thumb stroking the worn wood, her wordless refusal. Camera and composition return to it.
13. HANDHELD FROM THE HAND — held in human hands, a soft calm breathing sway, faint organic drift, intimate and close, alive but quiet and still, never aggressive never jittery never gimbal-smooth never tripod-locked.
14. LIP SYNC — THE ELDER's dim but visible face shows his lips and jaw clearly forming each Kazakh syllable on twos; ANA does not speak.

THE ELDER (Aksakal) from <<<image_2>>> speaks to ANA from <<<image_3>>>, the mother who has searched for her lost daughter for years and will not stop. He tells her plainly that so much time has passed, that the wolves have cost the people many lives, that it is time for her to stop. ANA does not answer. She sits holding and slowly turning her lost daughter's small wooden toy in her hands. Her silence and her hands are her refusal. The scene ends on that refusal, wordless and unshakable.
2. FRAME-BY-FRAME HAND-DRAWN FEEL — every frame looks painted by hand, a gentle constant boil in the painted lines and brushstrokes, texture and contours subtly redrawn each frame, never frozen, never mechanically smooth, never interpolated or morphed. The hand of the animator visible in every frame, across the whole scene.
3. LENS AND FOCAL LENGTH — anamorphic cinema lenses, shot like real film. Each shot has its own focal length: the wide two-shot on a ~35mm for natural perspective holding both figures and the room; the coverage on the Elder on a ~50mm normal lens for an honest undistorted portrait; the insert of the hands on a ~85mm with a shallow focus so the background falls soft; the close on Ana on a ~85mm portrait lens for gentle compression and intimacy. Keep any shallow depth of field SOFT and SUBTLE, a gentle painterly fall-off of the background, never a strong photographic bokeh blur that would break the hand-drawn look.
4. LIGHT, SHADOW AND EXPOSURE — evening after sunset, a deeply LOW-KEY interior dominated by SOFT SHADOW: about 80 percent of the frame falls into gentle deep shadow, with only about 20 percent softly lit by the last weak afterglow of dusk seeping down through the round shanyrak opening above. Mostly darkness, a small quiet pool and edges of soft dim light. CRUCIAL: the shadows are SOFT and rich, full of subtle tone and detail in the darkness, NOT flat dead black, NOT crushed — gentle gradations within the dark. And although most of the frame is shadow, the small lit portion falls where it matters so the characters' faces and the key details stay clearly visible and readable — faces always legible within the gloom, never a black void. The light is VERY SOFT, diffuse, dim, NOT directional. ABSOLUTELY NO visible light rays, NO shafts, NO beams, NO god rays, NO hard streaks, NO volumetric light — cheap AI slop. The dusk light fades in softly from above with soft feathered edges, no hard line. Deep soft shadow as the dominant tone, a little soft light for the faces. No warm glow, no bounce from carpet, no fire, no lamp.
5. WHITE BALANCE AND COLOR — correct natural white balance, neutral and true, NOT a heavy blue color cast, NOT an electric-blue night filter, only very slightly cool as natural dusk but neutral overall. White and pale things believable near-white where the light touches them — ANA's head cloth soft off-white, the ELDER's beard natural grey-white, felt neutral. Muted, desaturated, warm earthy darkness, deep and dim, true neutral balance, like a properly graded low-key film night interior, never the fake uniform blue tint of AI footage.
6. THE ELDER'S CHARACTER — a wise, firm, dignified elder. He does NOT whine, plead, or beg for pity, NOT weepy or self-pitying. He speaks the truth as it is — calm, steady, grounded, with the quiet authority of an old man who has earned the right to say a hard thing. Bitterness and the weight of years, but no weakness, no tears, no trembling. Plainly: enough, accept it. Strength and hard-earned wisdom, not sorrow.
7. ACTING IS EVERYTHING — long heavy silences between his phrases, restraint, no big gestures. Emotion reads through the visible faces, the eyes, posture, the angle and weight of the head, shoulders, hands, breath and stillness, drawn on twos as held painted poses. Give the pauses real time.
8. THE ELDER'S PERFORMANCE AND FACIAL MICRO-ACTING — he sits upright and composed in profile, head level, dignified, his lined face dim but clearly visible, speaking slowly and evenly. His face is alive with restrained micro-expression drawn on twos as held poses: slow heavy blinks of tired old eyes; his grey brows moving with weight — drawing together in a faint grave furrow on the hard words, lifting just slightly in weariness in the pauses; the deep lines of his brow and around his eyes shifting; small movements of the mouth and jaw beneath the beard as he forms words and presses his lips between phrases; the faint tightening of the eyes of a man carrying old sorrow. All of it grave, controlled, dignified — the micro-acting of calm authority, never twitchy, never weepy, never pleading. His steady gaze and upright bearing carry his strength.
9. ANA'S PERFORMANCE AND FACIAL MICRO-ACTING — she sits folded down over her hands, head bowed low, her worn grief-hollowed face dim and shadowed under her head cloth but STILL VISIBLE and readable, never a black void — her lowered eyes, features and quiet grief seen. Restrained micro-expression on twos: a faint tightening of the jaw, slow heavy blinks, the brows drawing faintly together, eyes glistening but never spilling, breath catching once. Her hands slowly turn the little wooden toy, her thumb stroking its worn surface. At his hardest words her hands still and close around it. She never speaks.
10. THE WOODEN TOY — her lost daughter's keepsake: a small simple hand-carved wooden toy, a little carved animal figure, worn smooth and darkened from years of being held, a humble child's plaything the mother made or kept. Small, precious, the only thing of her daughter she has left. She cradles and turns it in her hands, her thumb running over the smooth worn wood.
11. SECONDARY ACTION ON EVERYTHING THAT MOVES — follow-through and overlapping action drawn on twos, the hallmark of real hand animation. THE ELDER'S HAT: he wears a tall Kazakh felt hat with WIDE SOFT FLUFFY FUR BRIM (a broad fur-edged kalpak as in <<<image_2>>>) — this thick soft fur must be ALIVE and clearly MOVING: the long soft hairs and tufts of the fur brim sway, ripple, lift and settle with delayed secondary motion every time he moves, turns, tilts or nods his head, the fur lagging a beat behind the head and resettling softly, never stiff, never frozen, never a rigid solid shape — it is soft animal fur that flows and jiggles gently with each movement. THE ELDER'S BEARD: his long grey-white beard swings and settles with its own weight as he speaks and his jaw and head move. THE ELDER'S HAIR: loose grey strands at his temples drift and resettle. THE ELDER'S ROBE: the wide cuffs, skirts, collar and gold-trimmed edges of his heavy chapan shift, fold and settle with delayed motion as he breathes and shifts; his breath-vapor curls faintly. ANA: her white head cloth and kimeshek ends and chapan folds stir softly with her breath and small movements, loose hair drifts, breath-vapor curls. Dust floats softly. Nothing rigid — every soft material, ESPECIALLY the fluffy fur of the Elder's hat, lags, overlaps and settles a beat after the body, all drawn on twos, alive and hand-drawn.
12. THE TOY IS THE HEART — ANA's hands slowly, continuously turn and cradle her daughter's small carved wooden toy, her thumb stroking the worn wood, her wordless refusal. Camera and composition return to it.
13. HANDHELD FROM THE HAND — held in human hands, a soft calm breathing sway, faint organic drift, intimate and close, alive but quiet and still, never aggressive never jittery never gimbal-smooth never tripod-locked.
14. LIP SYNC — THE ELDER's dim but visible face shows his lips and jaw clearly forming each Kazakh syllable on twos; ANA does not speak.

2. STEPPED STOP-MOTION MOVEMENT — this is the most important rule: ALL character motion is on twos at 12fps, stepped and slightly choppy like classic hand-drawn animation and stop-motion. Head turns happen as a short series of held poses snapping one to the next, not a smooth glide. Blinks are two or three held drawings (open, half, shut) snapping, not a smooth eyelid slide. Mouth shapes for speech snap pose to pose. Hand movements step. The whole performance has the strobing, deliberate, pose-to-pose rhythm of animation on twos — NEVER the smooth fluid interpolated motion of high frame rate AI video. Keep movements small and slow, but stepped.
3. SHOT/REVERSE-SHOT DIALOGUE COVERAGE — cut as a classic dialogue: an establishing two-shot, then over-the-shoulder reverse angles cutting between the two as he speaks and she receives, then a close on each for the emotional beats. 5. VERY SOFT, diffuse, dim, NOT directional. ABSOLUTELY NO visible light rays, NO shafts, NO beams, NO god rays, NO hard streaks, NO volumetric light — cheap AI slop. Soft feathered edges, no hard line. No warm glow, no bounce from carpet, no fire, no lamp.

Muted, desaturated, warm earthy darkness, deep and dim, true neutral balance, like a properly graded low-key film night interior, never the fake uniform blue tint of AI footage.
7. THE ELDER'S CHARACTER — a wise, firm, dignified elder. He does NOT whine, plead, or beg for pity, NOT weepy or self-pitying. He speaks the truth as it is — calm, steady, grounded, with the quiet authority of an old man who has earned the right to say a hard thing. Bitterness and the weight of years, but no weakness, no tears, no trembling. Plainly: enough, accept it. Strength and hard-earned wisdom, not sorrow.
8. ACTING AND PAUSES — long heavy silences between his phrases, restraint, no big gestures. Emotion reads through the visible faces, eyes, posture, head angle, shoulders, hands, breath and stillness — all in stepped poses on twos. Give the pauses real time.
9. 10. ANA'S FACIAL MICRO-ACTING — she does not look at him, eyes down on the toy, her worn grief-hollowed face dim but visible and readable, never a black void. DIRECTOR'S NOTES:
1. THE SCENE — a STRONG BLIZZARD. On the snowy ground at the edge of the winter pastures lies the bloodied carcass of a sheep, half-buried in drifting snow, dark blood frozen into the snow around it — and over it, feeding, stands A SINGLE WOLF. It eats calmly, unhurried, utterly indifferent to the storm — until something stops it. No other wolves visible — whether it is alone, the storm hides. The first sign of the attacks, the threat itself in frame. The calm of the predator is the horror.
2. HEAVY BLIZZARD, LOW VISIBILITY — visibility only about 20 percent: dense driving snow streams through the frame, the world dissolves into a white-grey storm haze within meters, NO treeline, NO horizon, NO sky — only the near ground readable. The storm conceals everything beyond — the wolf and the carcass are the ONLY dark readable shapes in the white.
3. CAMERA LAW (Lubezki mechanics) — ONE SINGLE CONTINUOUS LONG TAKE, no cuts: one slow MOTIVATED move — the camera starts VERY LOW, almost lying on the snow surface, and SLOWLY, continuously RISES upward and forward like a person straightening up to look — and the moment the WOLF resolves out of the snow, the rise HALTS at a low crouched height and FREEZES there: the motivated stillness of someone who has just seen a predator and dares not move. The handheld breathing sway tightens, careful, almost held breath, a faint tremor. The camera is a LIVING HUMAN PRESENCE immersed inside the storm, spindrift streaking close past the lens, the wind faintly buffeting the frame. Natural storm light only. Never gimbal-smooth, never mechanical, never tripod-locked. Never rising above the wolf's level.
4. THE WOLF'S FEEDING — REAL ANIMAL PHYSICS, all stepped on twos at 12fps: the wolf stands over the carcass, braces its forepaws into the body, clamps its jaws into the flesh and TEARS a chunk free with a hard backward WRENCH of its head, neck and whole body — and the carcass JERKS and drags with each pull, cause and effect visible; then it lifts its head and GULPS the torn piece down in stepped swallows, throat working, muzzle dark with muted blood; then a PAUSE — ears swiveling — then it lowers its head and tears again. Methodical, unhurried, indifferent. The tearing wrenches are sharp stepped motions snapping pose to pose; the stillness between them is absolute.
5. THE FINAL BEAT — ALERT, LISTENING — after a feeding cycle, the wolf suddenly SNAPS its head UP from the carcass and FREEZES, its whole body going rigid and still mid-motion — it has heard something. Head lifted and turned slightly to the side, ears pricked and naming a direction, pale eyes fixed off into the storm, a last shred of flesh in its jaws or muzzle dark with blood, breath-vapor huffing and tearing away. It holds this alert listening pose, utterly motionless except for fur and breath-vapor in the wind, staring and listening off-frame into the blizzard at something WE CANNOT SEE — the unseen threat or the unseen pack. The eyeline leads out of frame into the white. Hold on this frozen listening wolf to the end. What it heard is never shown.
6. FOCUS — the focus belongs to the WOLF AND THE CARCASS as one point of attention: as the camera rises they resolve out of the storm and focus HOLDS on them, a soft subtle painterly fall-off, the foreground snow and the storm beyond melting into white haze, never a strong photographic bokeh that breaks the hand-drawn look.
7. COMPOSITION LAW (the frame serves the story) — SPACE: flat, compressed, shallow — the blizzard erases depth, no horizon, no way out. LINE: the spindrift draws fast horizontal storm lines; the wolf's hunched back a tense arched line over the carcass, and on the final beat its lifted head and fixed gaze a sharp diagonal eyeline pointing off-frame into the storm. SHAPE: the dead sheep one soft ROUNDED mass — the wolf over it ANGULAR and tense; angular over rounded. TONE: maximum tonal contrast at the point of attention — one combined dark mass on the near-white storm field. COLOR: near-monochrome desaturated storm greys; the dark muted red-brown of blood — on the snow and the wolf's muzzle — the ONLY color accent. MOVEMENT: contrast of movement as drama — the storm streaming fast, horizontal, smooth; the camera's slow rise halting into stillness; the wolf's sharp stepped tearing against its dead-still pauses, then the final snap-to-alert and total freeze. RHYTHM: tear — gulp — silence, then the rhythm BROKEN by the sudden alert head-lift and held stillness. CONTRAST & AFFINITY: restrained early-arc intensity — quiet dread with the threat present, ending on a held note of new alarm, not climax.
8. FRAMED INK STAGING (the shot read as masses) — read the frame as masses first: ONE combined dark mass low in a vast light field — angular predator over rounded prey. CONCEAL, DON'T REVEAL: the storm hides whether the pack is near, and on the final beat the wolf hears what we cannot — the unseen is the horror. CAMERA HEIGHT AS EMOTION: from helpless ground level rising only to a low crouched height, at the wolf's own level, never above, never dominant. LARGE VS SMALL: the vast formless storm against the small dark scene.
9. LIGHT — dim cold storm light inside a blizzard, flat, soft, directionless, no sun, no hard-edged shadows, no rays, no beams, no god rays. Correct neutral white balance, only slightly cool, NOT a blue cast, NOT an electric-blue filter, muted desaturated palette, the snow a soft storm-grey white, the blood dark muted red-brown, never bright, never glossy.
10. As ANA climbs one-armed with her infant, her foot dislodges a rock slab; the slab falls toward little UMAI below; and a WOLF leaps and SHOVES UMAI clear WITH ITS BODY an instant before the slab hits — the wolf SAVES her. 2. THE CAUSAL CHAIN — stage each link on screen, cause before effect, on twos: (a) ANA's foot comes down on a ledge high on the cliff, the ledge CRACKS and BREAKS under her weight; (b) a heavy SLAB breaks loose and FALLS straight down toward UMAI — the falling rock the through-line; (c) UMAI stands directly below, looking up; (d) from the side a WOLF LAUNCHES and SLAMS its shoulder and body into UMAI — NOT its jaws, NOT a bite — knocking her sideways clear; (e) the slab CRASHES into the snow exactly where she stood, a burst of powder snow on twos; (f) UMAI tumbles unhurt among the wolves. 3. THE WOLF SAVES WITH ITS BODY — CRITICAL: the first wolf strikes UMAI with its shoulder/flank, a SHOVE, mouth NOT on her, no bite, no seize — a rescue read as a body-slam. For one instant it LOOKS like an attack — then the rock smashes the empty snow and we understand. Play the shock-reversal.

DIRECTOR'S NOTES:
1. THE SCENE — a MEMORY, the day everything was lost. Cold fog, snow and wind at the foot of a steep cliff. ANA, fleeing with her two children, exhausted and freezing and in a hurry, cradles her swaddled infant and must climb. She kneels before her small daughter UMAI to leave her below a moment — and makes the vow that haunts the whole film. The tender, terrible calm before catastrophe. Play it for love and dread.
2. PHYSICAL STATE — RUNS THROUGH ALL THE ACTING: they are FREEZING, EXHAUSTED and HURRYING, and it must read on their faces and bodies in every beat. COLD: faces stiff and wind-burned, cheeks and noses raw red, eyes watering and stinging from the wind, lips pale and trembling, fine shivers running through their shoulders, breath coming in visible ragged clouds, hands stiff and clumsy with cold. EXHAUSTION: heavy-lidded tired eyes, faces drawn and spent, shoulders sagging with fatigue, movements weary and effortful, the deep tiredness of people who have fled a long way. HURRY: a nervous urgency under everything — ANA keeps the goodbye fast and pressed, glancing up at the cliff and around at the storm, no time, she must go; even her tenderness is rushed, snatched. All of this on twos as held poses — stiff cold faces, weary bodies, urgent glances.
3. FACIAL ACTING — THE HEART OF THE SHOT, faces clearly LIT and READABLE, never black voids, full visible micro-acting in stepped held poses on twos, given TIME: ANA fights a quiet war on her cold tired face — terror underneath, tenderness forced over it for the child's sake, exhaustion and cold weighing on it: her wind-stung eyes well and glisten, her brow knits with fear then smooths gentle for UMAI, her cold-trembling chin she steadies, her pale lips try a small reassuring softness while her jaw is tight, she swallows hard, she shivers. UMAI: wide frightened watering eyes in a raw cold little face, searching her mother for safety and warmth, lip trembling with cold and fear, a tiny uncertain nod, shivering, trusting completely. The whole scene lives in these two cold tired faces.
4. THE BEAT OF DOUBT — CRUCIAL BEAT, after UMAI asks if she will be abandoned, AND SHE DOES NOT LOOK AWAY: the child's question pierces ANA's brave mask while she is looking straight into UMAI's eyes. The doubt moves THROUGH her WITHOUT breaking the eye contact — she holds her daughter's gaze the whole time. For a held moment the fear surfaces in her eyes even as she keeps looking at UMAI: her reassuring expression falters, a flicker of the dark thought that she might not come back rises up behind her eyes, her wind-stung eyes glistening harder, her brow tightening, a cold breath catching, her cold chin trembling once — all while her eyes stay locked on her daughter's, unable and unwilling to look away from the child she is afraid she may not return to. Then — an effort of will: she steadies, draws a shaking cold breath, and still holding UMAI's eyes, chooses to make the vow ANYWAY, in spite of the doubt. The doubt and the choice both happen in unbroken eye contact — that is what makes it hurt. Played in held stepped poses on twos, readable but restrained.

A lone white yurt on flat snowy steppe, a herd of dark horses running in orbital formation around it, fire burning at the yurt's base and doorway, dark smoke rising and spiraling. Deep grey sky, pale white steppe dissolving at every edge into cold void. The palette is cold grey, near-black, and white — the fire at center the only warm color in the world. STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: applying any warm tone to the horses or the steppe outside the fire's immediate radius.

Lighting: the fire inside the yurt is the only warm light source — the only red, the only orange, the only heat anywhere in this world. It glows at the base and through the doorway, spilling a small red-amber wash onto the snow directly around the structure. Everything else: flat cold grey, light rising from the snow. The sky is dark grey pressing down. The smoke is black-grey and heavy. The horses are dark shapes against white — no warmth on them. The fire draws the eye because it is the only color.

Atmosphere: no weather. No wind. The stillness of a place outside time. Breath vapor, if it exists, rises straight up and hangs without dispersing. The snow is undisturbed everywhere except the deep circular groove carved by the horses' repeated passes. The smoke rises straight up, then bends into the vortex of the horses' motion — drawn into their orbit — then straightens in the gap, then bends again as the next horse passes. The fire does not spread. The yurt does not collapse. Things in dreams burn forever.

DIRECTORIAL NOTE: Three shots, three relationships to the fire. The emotional structure is: beauty → obstruction → arrival. The dream pulls you toward the fire across all three shots — first you see it whole and far, then the horses block you from it, then you are inside and it is too late to matter. The zoom is continuous across all three shots, never stopping, the world getting slowly closer whether you consent to it or not.

From above the choppiness makes the circle look mechanical, like a clock, like a thing that cannot be stopped because it was never alive to begin with. The smoke spirals. The fire burns. The steppe ends at grey nothing in every direction. There is no world outside this circle.

As ANA climbs the snowy cliff one-armed with her infant, her foot dislodges a slab of packed snow high on the slope; the slab breaks loose and roars down as an AVALANCHE toward little UMAI below; UMAI sees it coming and reacts in terror; the avalanche engulfs her and sweeps her away. UMAI'S PERFORMANCE — CRUCIAL, SHE IS NOT A PROP, SHE MUST REACT AND ACT, NOT STAND STILL — a clear readable ARC OF FEAR, her face and body fully alive on twos as held stepped poses, a beat on each: (a) WAITING — she stands alone where her mother left her, small and lost and cold, shivering, hugging herself, looking up after her mother, her little face anxious and uncertain, breath-vapor puffing; (b) ALARM — she hears the deep rumble, her whole body flinches, her head SNAPS round toward the sound, her eyes go WIDE, she freezes searching for it; (c) HORROR — she SEES the white wall of the avalanche roaring down at her and her face BREAKS OPEN in terror, eyes huge, mouth opening in a scream, her small body recoiling backward, her hands flying up toward her face and out toward her mother; (d) PANIC — she shrinks and twists as if to run or shield herself, a tiny terrified figure throwing up her arms, an instant before the white engulfs her. DIRECTOR'S NOTES:
1. THE SCENE — the catastrophe, the heart of the whole story, and it MUST READ through a precise CHAIN OF CAUSE AND EFFECT, with composition and camera telling the cruel story. As ANA climbs the snowy cliff one-armed with her infant, her foot dislodges a slab of packed snow high on the slope; the slab breaks loose and roars DOWN the cliff as an AVALANCHE toward little UMAI below; UMAI, looking up after her mother, sees it coming down at her and reacts in terror; the avalanche engulfs her and sweeps her away. ANA, high above, sees it and screams, helpless. No wolves, no rock — a slab of mountain snow becomes an avalanche from above, and the child is taken by it. ANA is the unwitting cause from above; the mountain itself takes her daughter.
2. UMAI'S PERFORMANCE — CRUCIAL, SHE IS NOT A PROP, SHE MUST REACT AND ACT, NOT STAND STILL — a clear readable ARC OF FEAR, her face and body fully alive on twos as held stepped poses, a beat on each: (a) WAITING — she stands alone at the foot of the cliff where her mother left her, small and lost and cold, shivering, hugging herself, her head tilted UP watching her mother climb away above her, her little face anxious; (b) ALARM — a deep rumble from ABOVE, she flinches, her upturned eyes go WIDE as she stares UP the slope at the sound, searching the cliff above; (c) HORROR — she SEES the white wall of the avalanche pouring DOWN the cliff straight at her from above, and her face BREAKS OPEN in terror, eyes huge staring UP, mouth opening in a scream, her small body recoiling and craning back as it bears down from overhead, her hands flying up toward it and toward her mother above; (d) PANIC — she shrinks and twists as if to flee, throwing up her arms over her head against the white coming down, a tiny terrified figure, an instant before it engulfs her. She is REACTING to the avalanche descending FROM ABOVE — looking UP, never sideways, never passive. Her terror is the emotional core of this shot — play it BIG and READABLE on her small upturned face.
3. THE CAUSAL CHAIN — stage each link on screen, cause before effect, on twos: (a) ANA's foot comes down on a thick ledge of packed SNOW high on the cliff and the snow slab CRACKS and BREAKS away under her weight, a fracture line shooting across the slope; (b) the broken SLAB OF SNOW slides and then ROARS DOWN the cliff face as an AVALANCHE, a growing churning wall of snow descending — the avalanche the through-line, follow it DOWN the slope; (c) UMAI below, looking UP, SEES it coming down and reacts in terror; (d) the descending AVALANCHE reaches her and ENGULFS her — a churning white wave breaking over the tiny terrified figure from above, swallowing her; (e) UMAI is swept off her feet and CARRIED AWAY in the torrent of snow, a small dark shape tumbling and vanishing into the churning white as the avalanche pours on past and away downslope. Every cause visible: the foot fractures the snow slab, the slab becomes the avalanche pouring down, the avalanche from above takes the child.
4. THE AVALANCHE — REAL PHYSICS AND WEIGHT, the snow stepped on twos, ALWAYS MOVING DOWNSLOPE FROM ABOVE: a packed snow slab fracturing and breaking loose high up; the avalanche building as it descends the cliff — a churning tumbling wall of snow blocks and powder, heavy and fast and unstoppable, a billowing cloud of snow-powder rising off its front, pouring DOWN toward the child below; it breaks over UMAI like a wave from above; it sweeps her away and pours on down and past, throwing up great bursts and clouds of snow-powder (drawn snow-spray and powder on twos). Massive, violent, indifferent, coming from above.
5. UMAI IS TAKEN — the avalanche engulfs and carries UMAI off, NOT crushing her in gore — she is swept up and buried and tumbled away in the white torrent, a small dark shape (the only color her clothing) vanishing into the churning snow, gone into the white. 6. HARD CUT to SHOT 3 — BELOW, WIDE, ~35mm, aggressive handheld. COMPOSITION (the downward pour): the avalanche pours on DOWN the slope and across along a strong descending DIAGONAL line of dynamics, a vast churning river of snow and billowing powder cloud sweeping away downslope into fog and blizzard, the place where UMAI stood now buried and erased, the pale churning white and fog the negative space that has swallowed her. Snow-powder billowing and bursting on twos. She is gone into the white, taken by the mountain.

HARD CUT to SHOT 4 — ANA ON THE CLIFF, ~50mm, aggressive handheld, horizon reeling. COMPOSITION (big-versus-small, the cruel permanent distance): ANA TINY and helpless high on the vast rock-and-snow face clinging one-armed with her dark-blue swaddled infant, the enormous cold cliff and pale fog and storm and the raw avalanche scar below dwarfing her, the churning white torrent and powder cloud far below at the very bottom of frame where her daughter vanished — the tall vertical distance between them, the path the avalanche took, now permanent and unbridgeable, dominant negative space of loss. "UMAI!!! U-MA-AI!!!"

Her cry torn away by the wind. Far below, the avalanche and her daughter are gone into fog and churning snow. Hold on her tiny helpless figure and the vast empty white below where UMAI was. End.

Style: STOP-MOTION ANIMATION — stepped, frame-by-frame motion brought to a HAND-PAINTED 2D. True 12 frames per second, ANIMATED ON TWOS: 12 distinct hand-painted drawings per second, each pose held two frames then snapping to the next, never gliding. Constant painterly BOIL — brushstrokes and outlines subtly alive frame to frame. NO smooth interpolation, NO motion blur, NO morphing. STRICTLY NO SMOOTH MOTION ON THE HORSES — every leg, every mane strand, every tail snaps between held drawings at 12fps. The choppiness is visible. The horses do not glide — they stutter forward in frozen increments, like a zoetrope, like a flipbook. 8K IMAX, hand-painted oil-brush texture on every drawing, brushstrokes shifting and redrawn frame to frame, line jitter and boil between frames. No 3D render, no game engine, no CGI smoothness. Subtle chromatic aberration — faint color fringing at high-contrast edges, most visible where dark horse shapes cross the pale snow. The 12 principles of animation throughout.

THIS IS A DREAM. Dream logic governs. Normal cinematography rules suspended.

CHARACTER REFERENCE IS ABSOLUTE — faces and designs from reference images exactly 1-to-1. Reference always overrides text description.

Lighting: the fire inside the yurt is the only warm light source — the only red, the only orange, the only heat anywhere in this world. It glows at the base and through the doorway, spilling a small red-amber wash onto the snow directly around the structure. Everything else: flat cold grey, light rising from the snow. The sky is dark grey pressing down. The smoke is black-grey and heavy. The horses are dark shapes against white — no warmth on them. The fire draws the eye because it is the only color.

Atmosphere: no weather. No wind. The stillness of a place outside time. Breath vapor, if it exists, rises straight up and hangs without dispersing. The snow is undisturbed everywhere except the deep circular groove carved by the horses' repeated passes. The smoke rises straight up, then bends into the vortex of the horses' motion — drawn into their orbit — then straightens in the gap, then bends again as the next horse passes. The fire does not spread. The yurt does not collapse. Things in dreams burn forever.

Audio: Shot 1 — the circular hoofbeat rhythm only. Regular, hypnotic, slightly wrong in its regularity. Shot 2 — hooves deafening at close range, and in the gaps between passing horses: the crackle of fire, audible and real. Shot 3 — hooves receding, gone. Only the fire. No music. No dialogue. No subtitles.

DIRECTORIAL NOTE: Three shots, three relationships to the fire. The emotional structure is: beauty → obstruction → arrival. The dream pulls you toward the fire across all three shots — first you see it whole and far, then the horses block you from it, then you are inside and it is too late to matter. The zoom is continuous across all three shots, never stopping, the world getting slowly closer whether you consent to it or not.

SHOT 1 — GOD'S-EYE WIDE — the vision reveals itself. Duration: approx. 5 seconds.

Camera: elevated, looking down at a steep angle, the yurt small at center, the orbital ring of horses around it visible in its full geometry. The horizon is level — wrong, in this film where the horizon is never level. That wrongness is the first signal that something is different. Very slow zoom in begins — imperceptible frame to frame, only readable over time.

The circle almost looks beautiful from here. The dark horses making a perfect ring around the white yurt, the only red in the world at the center, the black smoke spiraling upward. The distance is the trap — at this remove it reads as order, as pattern, almost as ritual. The viewer does not yet know to be afraid. The horses stutter in their 12fps gallop — the circle lurches forward in discrete choppy increments, each horse snapping between frozen poses, the ring advancing like a zoetrope strip. From above the choppiness makes the circle look mechanical, like a clock, like a thing that cannot be stopped because it was never alive to begin with. The smoke spirals. The fire burns. The steppe ends at grey nothing in every direction. There is no world outside this circle.

Secondary action: manes and tails snap between held positions — not flowing, snapping. The circular groove in the snow is already deep and dark, worn to near-earth by how many passes we do not know.

SHOT 2 — GROUND LEVEL, OUTSIDE THE CIRCLE — the horses as wall. Duration: approx. 5 seconds.

Camera: suddenly at ground level, at the edge of the orbital path — the dream has moved us without warning. We are standing just outside the circle, facing inward. The horses stream past left-to-right at full gallop, close, their dark bodies filling the left half of frame as they pass — massive, choppy, stuttering, enormous at this proximity. Their legs snap between extended and tucked in hard 12fps cuts, no smoothing, the stutter nearly strobing as they flash past in sequence.

And in the gaps between the passing horses — the yurt. Visible in flashes. The fire at its base, red-orange and real, there and gone and there again as each horse's body crosses in front of it and uncovers it. The rhythm: horse — fire — horse — fire — horse. We can see it burning. We cannot get through. There is no gap between horses wide enough to pass. The zoom continues — we are getting closer to the circle's edge, but the horses fill every gap as we approach, the wall of dark bodies thickening. The fire crackles in the half-second windows between passing animals — heard and seen and then covered again.

This is the nightmare's core: the fire is visible, close, real — and the horses are not threatening us, not even acknowledging us. They simply run their circle and their running is the barrier. It does not matter to them that the yurt is burning. It has never mattered. They have always been running.

The choppy 12fps stutter of the horses matters most here — the strobe of dark bodies at this proximity is almost violent, the hard pose-to-pose snap of each animal passing filling and emptying the frame in rapid succession.

Camera: held. Still. The zoom is the only movement. The horses come to us.

SHOT 3 — GROUND LEVEL, INSIDE THE CIRCLE — arrival. Duration: approx. 5 seconds.

Camera: we are inside now. We do not know how. The horses are behind us — their hoofbeats audible but receding, as if we passed through a membrane. The yurt is directly ahead, close, the fire at its doorway filling the lower center of frame. The red-orange glow is larger here than it has been in either previous shot — the only warm thing, and we are close enough to feel it would be warm if this were real. The smoke rises straight up above the crown into the still dead air.

The zoom has almost stopped — we have arrived, and arrival has its own stillness. Almost stopped, but not quite. The dream still pulls. Barely.

Nothing happens. The yurt burns. The fire steps through its 12fps flicker — each flame shape a distinct held drawing, snap, snap, snap, the light shifting in choppy increments on the surrounding snow. The smoke rises in stepped increments, each frame a new drawing of the curl advancing upward. The yurt is not collapsing. The fire is not spreading. It is simply burning, as it has been burning, as it will always be burning.

We arrived. There is nothing to do here. There was never anything to do here. The dream shows you the fire and then it shows you that being here changes nothing.

Hold. Hold. Then the shot ends.

Camera: the zoom barely moves. Almost still. The fire flickers in its stopped-motion stutter. That is all.

GEOGRAPHY OF THE SCENE — LOCK THIS, it is the key to the shot: the CLIFF is IN FRONT OF UMAI and rises UP before her. ANA climbed UP that cliff and is high on it. UMAI stands at the foot of the cliff FACING IT, looking UP at the cliff after her mother. The AVALANCHE comes DOWN that SAME cliff — the very cliff UMAI is facing and looking up at — and pours DOWN toward her, straight into her, FACE TO FACE. So UMAI and the avalanche are FACING EACH OTHER: she looks up at the cliff, and the white wall comes down off that cliff right at her. She SEES it coming because she is looking right at it. The danger comes from IN FRONT, from the cliff she faces, from where her mother is — NOT from behind her, NEVER from behind her. The camera must be placed to the SIDE of UMAI or just OVER HER SHOULDER toward the cliff, so that in one frame we see BOTH her face turned up toward the cliff AND the avalanche pouring down off that cliff toward her — the child and the avalanche facing each other. Do NOT put the avalanche behind her back.

DIRECTOR'S NOTES:
1. THE SCENE — the catastrophe, the heart of the whole story, and it MUST READ through a precise CHAIN OF CAUSE AND EFFECT, with composition and camera telling the cruel story. As ANA climbs the snowy cliff one-armed with her infant, her foot dislodges a slab of packed snow high on the slope; the slab breaks loose and roars DOWN the cliff as an AVALANCHE straight toward little UMAI, who stands at the foot of the cliff facing it and looking up after her mother; UMAI sees it coming down at her and freezes in quiet fear; the avalanche engulfs her and sweeps her away. ANA, high above, sees it and screams, helpless. No wolves, no rock — a slab of mountain snow becomes an avalanche pouring down the cliff, and the child facing that cliff is taken by it.
2. CAMERA LAW (LUBEZKI handheld craft, applied WITHIN each shot — hard cuts between shots stay, but each shot is shot like Lubezki) — every shot is ONE continuous, motivated, flowing HANDHELD move, never static, never locked: (a) HANDHELD HUMAN PRESENCE — the camera is held in human hands, a living breathing presence inside the scene, a soft organic sway and drift, jolts and corrections, buffeted by the wind gusts, never gimbal-smooth, never tripod-locked, never mechanical; in the catastrophe beats the handheld is aggressive and urgent, in the held moments it breathes; (b) CONTINUOUS MOTIVATED MOVEMENT — each shot moves for a reason driven by the action: it climbs with ANA, it tilts and falls following the avalanche, it cranes and reframes with UMAI, it reels with the scream — one fluid motivated camera move per shot, not a fixed frame; (c) IMMERSED IN THE ELEMENT — the camera is INSIDE the storm with the characters: blowing snow and spindrift streak close past the lens, fog drifts through the frame, the avalanche's powder bursts toward camera, we are in it, not observing from outside; (d) WIDE IMMERSIVE FRAMING — favor wide, close, enveloping framing that puts us bodily in the space, the vast cliff and storm wrapping around the figures; (e) NATURAL LIGHT ONLY — lit only by the existing dim grey storm light, no artificial light, no rays, no beams; (f) PALETTE FROM THE SCENE — the cold grey-white of the storm and snow is the whole palette. This Lubezki handheld craft runs through ALL FOUR shots.
3. UMAI'S PERFORMANCE — QUIET FEAR, RESTRAINED, NOT A BIG REACTION, NO SCREAM — she does not cry out, she does not flail; she is a small frightened child who FREEZES. A clear but understated arc, her face and body alive on twos as held stepped poses, a beat on each: (a) WAITING — she stands alone at the foot of the cliff FACING IT, small and lost and cold, shivering, hugging herself, her head tilted UP watching her mother climb the cliff above her, her little face anxious; (b) UNEASE — a deep rumble from the cliff in front of her, she goes still, her upturned eyes widening as she looks UP the cliff she faces, uneasy, not understanding yet; (c) FRIGHTENED REALIZATION — she SEES the white wall of the avalanche pouring DOWN the cliff straight at her, coming face to face with her, and her eyes go WIDE with fear and her small face fills with fright — but quietly, frozen: lips parting slightly, breath catching, her little body going rigid and shrinking down a little, a tiny frightened child staring up at what is bearing down on her, rooted to the spot, NOT screaming, NOT flailing; (d) the white reaches her — she barely flinches before the avalanche engulfs her. Keep her fear INTERNAL and STILL — wide frightened eyes, a frozen upturned face looking straight at the oncoming snow, the quiet terror of a child too frightened to move. Readable on her small face but never loud, never a scream. (NOTE: the painterly look, the rosy cold cheeks, the fur-trimmed hood and the quiet frightened upturned expression from the reference frame are right — keep that, just fix the geography so the avalanche is in front of her, off the cliff she faces, not behind her.)
4. THE CAUSAL CHAIN — stage each link on screen, cause before effect, on twos: (a) ANA's foot comes down on a thick ledge of packed SNOW high on the cliff and the snow slab CRACKS and BREAKS away under her weight, a fracture line shooting across the slope; (b) the broken SLAB OF SNOW slides and then ROARS DOWN the face of the cliff as an AVALANCHE, a growing churning wall of snow descending the cliff toward UMAI at its foot — the avalanche the through-line, follow it DOWN the cliff; (c) UMAI at the foot, facing the cliff and looking UP, SEES it coming down at her and freezes in quiet fright; (d) the descending AVALANCHE reaches her and ENGULFS her — a churning white wave breaking over the tiny still figure from the front, from the cliff she faces, swallowing her; (e) UMAI is swept off her feet and CARRIED AWAY in the torrent, a small dark shape tumbling and vanishing into the churning white as the avalanche pours on past. Every cause visible: the foot fractures the snow slab high up, the slab becomes the avalanche pouring down the cliff, the avalanche takes the child who faces that cliff.
5. THE AVALANCHE — REAL PHYSICS AND WEIGHT, the snow stepped on twos, ALWAYS POURING DOWN THE CLIFF THAT UMAI FACES, toward her, face to face: a packed snow slab fracturing and breaking loose high up on the cliff; the avalanche building as it descends the cliff face — a churning tumbling wall of snow blocks and powder, heavy and fast and unstoppable, a billowing cloud of snow-powder rising off its front, pouring DOWN the cliff toward the child at its foot; it breaks over UMAI like a wave from the front; it sweeps her away and pours on past, throwing up great bursts and clouds of snow-powder (drawn snow-spray and powder on twos). Massive, violent, indifferent, coming down the cliff she faces.
6. UMAI IS TAKEN — the avalanche engulfs and carries UMAI off, NOT crushing her in gore — she is swept up and buried and tumbled away in the white torrent, a small dark shape (the only color her clothing) vanishing into the churning snow, gone into the white. She is simply taken by the mountain. The mystery of whether she lives is left for the film.
7. ANA ABOVE SEES AND SCREAMS — high on the cliff, helpless, clinging one-armed with her baby, she looks DOWN and SEES the avalanche she loosed pour down the cliff and take UMAI at its foot, and reaches out and SCREAMS her daughter's name. FACIAL ACTING: her held composure SHATTERS — her face breaks open, eyes blown wide in horror, mouth tearing open, all the controlled tenderness from before exploding into raw terror, on twos as snapping held poses of a face coming apart. (Her scream is the one loud cry of the scene — the child stays silent, the mother screams.)
8. COMPOSITION LAW (the frame tells the story — RUPTURE, the opposite of the vow's affinity) — LINE: the cruel descending line of the avalanche pouring straight DOWN the cliff from ANA above onto UMAI at its foot — the line of doom running from mother at the top down the cliff to child at the bottom, the child facing up that line. SHAPE: the huge churning formless white mass of the avalanche pouring down the cliff and overwhelming the small rounded still child who faces it — the mountain swallowing her head-on. TONE: REVERSAL — the DARK small child engulfed by a huge BRIGHT white violent mass pouring down at her, the dark figure drowned in white; the child's frightened upturned face the focal point until the white takes her. MOVEMENT: contrast and high intensity — the fast violent down-pouring avalanche against the small still frightened child facing it and the slow helpless reach of the mother above. CONTRAST & AFFINITY: maximum CONTRAST and PEAK visual intensity — the rupture the vow's affinity has been saving for. SPACE: deep — the cliff receding up and away, the avalanche pouring down its face toward camera and child.
9. FRAMED INK STAGING (read as masses) — the small dark frightened child at the foot of the cliff ENGULFED and erased by the vast white churning mass pouring DOWN THE CLIFF SHE FACES — large-vs-small, the mountain's white violence descending head-on to swallow the tiny figure. CONCEAL: fog and the billowing snow-powder half-swallow the catastrophe, and the white torrent swallows UMAI completely. CAMERA HEIGHT: low and close and helpless at the child looking up the cliff as the white wall pours down at her; tiny and powerless at the mother above. LARGE VS SMALL: the small child and small distant mother against the vast cliff, the storm, the huge pouring avalanche.
10. WEATHER — FOG, SNOW, WIND, all smooth: low drifting fog across the cliff base, thick snow blown sideways in gusts, gusting wind dragging fog and snow and tearing breath-vapor, the catastrophe half-veiled and swallowed by the storm and the avalanche's powder cloud.
11. SECONDARY ACTION on twos — ANA's and UMAI's clothes hair and breath-vapor whipping, the dark-blue swaddled bundle shifting, the avalanche throwing up bursts and billowing clouds of snow-powder, snow blocks tumbling, all drawn on twos; fog and blowing snow smooth.
12. LIGHT — cold grey stormlight in fog and snow, flat soft directionless, no sun, no rays, no beams, no god rays, faces readable. Correct neutral white balance, NOT a blue filter, muted desaturated, snow soft storm-grey white, fog pale grey; bloodless — the child is taken by snow, not harmed on screen.

DIRECTOR'S NOTES:
1. THE SCENE — a MEMORY, the day everything was lost. Cold fog, snow and wind at the foot of a steep cliff. ANA, fleeing with her two children, exhausted and freezing and in a hurry, cradles her swaddled infant and must climb. She kneels before her small daughter UMAI to leave her below a moment — and makes the vow that haunts the whole film. The tender, terrible calm before catastrophe. Play it for love and dread.
2. PHYSICAL STATE — RUNS THROUGH ALL THE ACTING: they are FREEZING, EXHAUSTED and HURRYING, and it must read on their faces and bodies in every beat. COLD: faces stiff and wind-burned, cheeks and noses raw red, eyes watering and stinging from the wind, lips pale and trembling, fine shivers running through their shoulders, breath coming in visible ragged clouds, hands stiff and clumsy with cold. EXHAUSTION: heavy-lidded tired eyes, faces drawn and spent, shoulders sagging with fatigue, movements weary and effortful, the deep tiredness of people who have fled a long way. HURRY: a nervous urgency under everything — ANA keeps the goodbye fast and pressed, glancing up at the cliff and around at the storm, no time, she must go; even her tenderness is rushed, snatched. All of this on twos as held poses — stiff cold faces, weary bodies, urgent glances.
3. FACIAL ACTING — THE HEART OF THE SHOT, faces clearly LIT and READABLE, never black voids, full visible micro-acting in stepped held poses on twos, given TIME: ANA fights a quiet war on her cold tired face — terror underneath, tenderness forced over it for the child's sake, exhaustion and cold weighing on it: her wind-stung eyes well and glisten, her brow knits with fear then smooths gentle for UMAI, her cold-trembling chin she steadies, her pale lips try a small reassuring softness while her jaw is tight, she swallows hard, she shivers. UMAI: wide frightened watering eyes in a raw cold little face, searching her mother for safety and warmth, lip trembling with cold and fear, a tiny uncertain nod, shivering, trusting completely. The whole scene lives in these two cold tired faces.
4. THE BEAT OF DOUBT — CRUCIAL BEAT, after UMAI asks if she will be abandoned, AND SHE DOES NOT LOOK AWAY: the child's question pierces ANA's brave mask while she is looking straight into UMAI's eyes. The doubt moves THROUGH her WITHOUT breaking the eye contact — she holds her daughter's gaze the whole time. For a held moment the fear surfaces in her eyes even as she keeps looking at UMAI: her reassuring expression falters, a flicker of the dark thought that she might not come back rises up behind her eyes, her wind-stung eyes glistening harder, her brow tightening, a cold breath catching, her cold chin trembling once — all while her eyes stay locked on her daughter's, unable and unwilling to look away from the child she is afraid she may not return to. Then — an effort of will: she steadies, draws a shaking cold breath, and still holding UMAI's eyes, chooses to make the vow ANYWAY, in spite of the doubt. The doubt and the choice both happen in unbroken eye contact — that is what makes it hurt. Played in held stepped poses on twos, readable but restrained.
5. CAMERA LAW (height as emotion) — UMAI is small and is being left, so frame her from a slightly HIGH angle (a gentle downshot = her smallness, the one left behind). ANA is the protector the child looks up to, so frame her from a slightly LOW angle FROM UMAI'S EYELINE (a gentle upshot = mother as the child's whole towering world) — but her fear and exhaustion undercut the power. On THE BEAT OF DOUBT, a slow gentle PUSH-IN toward ANA's face isolating her private moment, but staying on her eyes locked to UMAI's. The vertical up/down eyeline between them quietly foreshadows the vertical separation to come. Intimate handheld, a soft breathing sway, close on the faces, alive, never gimbal-smooth, never tripod-locked.
6. COMPOSITION LAW (the frame tells the story — AFFINITY, the last moment of connection) — SPACE: shallow, intimate, the two pressed close in one pocket of space. LINE: soft curved lines, the two bodies and heads curving toward each other, leaning in, joined by the unbroken eyeline between them. SHAPE: ROUNDED, soft, warm — mother and child curl together into one rounded tender shape (rounded = warmth, love) against the ANGULAR jagged dark mass of the cliff behind (angular = threat). TONE: the two faces the lit focal point, a warm readable mass; the cliff and fog darker around them. COLOR: muted desaturated, the cold raw faces the warmest note in cold grey storm, the swaddled baby a single deep dark-blue note in her arms. MOVEMENT: the figures slow and weary and close, small shivers and ragged breath; the fog and snow drifting around them — stillness of connection inside the moving storm. RHYTHM: calm, held, tender, hurried at the edges, with the one catch of doubt. CONTRAST & AFFINITY: maximum AFFINITY and LOW visual intensity here — closeness, warmth, the last connection — saving all contrast and rupture for the catastrophe to come.
7. FRAMED INK STAGING (read as masses) — TRAP-FRAME the two figures TOGETHER in a soft pocket of light, held close, the dark angular cliff mass looming above and behind them as the threat. CONCEAL: the fog hides what waits. CAMERA HEIGHT AS EMOTION: down on the small child, up on the towering mother. LARGE VS SMALL: the small cold human pair against the vast dark cliff and storm.
8. THE INFANT IN HER ARMS — cradled in one arm against her chest, only a small dark-blue swaddled bundle stirring faintly; she touches UMAI with her free hand; when she climbs she presses the baby tight to her chest with one arm and climbs one-armed — the terrible difficulty, made worse by cold-stiff hands.
9. PACE — slow, weighted, tender, but hurried at the edges — the snatched held breath of a desperate, freezing, rushed goodbye.
10. SECONDARY ACTION on twos — ANA's kimeshek ends and chapan, UMAI's small coat and hair whipping in the wind with follow-through, the visible ragged breath-vapor of both curling and torn off by gusts, small cold shivers through their shoulders, the dark-blue swaddled bundle shifting faintly; fog and blowing snow smooth.
11. LIGHT — cold grey stormlight in fog and snow, flat soft directionless, no sun, no rays, no beams, no god rays, the faces caught readable in soft light. Correct neutral white balance, NOT a blue filter, muted desaturated, snow soft storm-grey white, fog pale grey.

SHOT 1 — TWO-SHOT into CLOSE SINGLES, ~50mm, intimate handheld, foot of the cliff in fog, snow and wind. COMPOSITION (affinity): ANA kneeling on the RIGHT cradling the dark-blue swaddled infant in one arm, UMAI small on the LEFT, the two curving close toward each other into one warm rounded shape trapped in a soft pocket of light, the dark angular cliff looming behind into fog, fog and blowing snow drifting smooth across the frame. Both freezing, exhausted, hurrying — stiff cold red faces, watering eyes, ragged breath-vapor, small shivers. Framed slightly LOW on ANA (towering mother) and slightly HIGH on UMAI (small, left behind) on the reverse beats. ANA takes UMAI's shoulder with her cold-stiff free hand, glances once up at the cliff in urgency, her cold tired face fighting fear behind tenderness on twos — wind-stung eyes welling, brow smoothing gentle, trembling chin steadied — and speaks low and quick and urgent, lips on twos:

"Osy jerde tūr. Eşqayida ketpe. Men qazır kelemin."

CLOSE on UMAI, framed slightly high, her wide frightened watering eyes in a raw cold little face searching up at her mother, lip trembling with cold, shivering, clutching ANA's sleeve, lips on twos:

"Sen meni alıp ketesiñ be?.. Meni tastamaisıñ ba?"

THE BEAT OF DOUBT — a slow gentle PUSH-IN on ANA's face, her eyes staying LOCKED on UMAI's, never looking away. The question pierces her: her reassuring look falters while she holds her daughter's gaze, the dark thought that she might not come back rising behind her wind-stung glistening eyes, her brow tightening, a cold breath catching, her chin trembling once — all in unbroken eye contact with the child, all in stepped held poses on twos. Then an effort of will: she steadies, draws a shaking cold breath, and still holding UMAI's eyes, chooses the vow anyway.

A held beat — then she leans in, their two heads forming one shape, and kisses UMAI on the cold forehead, holds her small raw face one beat, and says the vow, soft and certain over the doubt, lips on twos:

"Kelemin. Men sağan ärqashan kelemin."

Hold one last beat on UMAI's small trusting cold face looking up, a tiny shivering nod, gusts of snow and fog crossing between them. Camera close and breathing.

HARD CUT to SHOT 2 — WIDE, VERTICAL composition, ~35mm, handheld, the foot of the cliff. COMPOSITION (the story = separation): the steep dark cliff rising TALL through the whole frame into fog, ANA beginning to climb one-armed in the MIDDLE with the dark-blue swaddled infant pressed to her chest, climbing wearily with cold-stiff hands, small UMAI alone at the very BOTTOM on the snow looking up — the tall empty VERTICAL gap of cliff between them as dominant negative space, the height itself the wedge driving them apart, the line of the climb pulling upward away from the child. Framed to feel UMAI tiny and abandoned below, half-veiled and swallowed by drifting fog, shivering. ANA climbs in heavy weary stepped poses, chapan and bundle shifting with follow-through; UMAI watches from below, tiny, waiting, growing smaller. The cold storm closing. Hold on the cruel widening vertical distance. End.

DIRECTOR'S NOTES:
1. THE SCENE — moments after the avalanche. The roar is gone; the white has settled. ANA has come down to the foot of the cliff, to the vast field of churned avalanche snow that swallowed her daughter, and she DIGS — clawing through the broken snow with one hand, the swaddled infant clutched to her chest with the other, searching for UMAI and calling her name into the empty white. Grief in frantic action: desperate digging, hope against hopelessness, a mother tearing at the snow that took her child. This shot stays OPEN — she digs and calls and finds nothing, the camera holding on her tiny figure searching the endless white, no answer, no resolution. Grief has no end.
2. TONAL CONTRAST WITH THE CATASTROPHE — the avalanche was a roar of speed and violence; THIS is the aftermath: quieter, heavier, emptier, but with a rising desperation. Slow grief-stricken weight building into frantic clawing, the near-silence of the settled snow broken only by wind, the scrape of snow, and her cracked voice calling her daughter.
3. ANA'S PERFORMANCE — grief in action, fully readable on twos as held stepped poses: she drops to her knees in the churned snow and DIGS, clawing and flinging snow aside with her free hand, the swaddled baby pressed to her chest hampering her, her cold-stiff hand scrabbling, sinking into the deep loose snow; she stops, lifts her head, scans the white, calls out, listens — nothing — and digs again, faster, more frantic; her worn face clearly LIT and READABLE, never a black void — raw open grief and terror, eyes wild and brimming, brow torn, mouth shaking as she calls, breath ragged, but she does NOT collapse — she keeps digging, keeps searching, driven. The frantic hope and the dawning hopelessness both on her face.
4. THE BABY HAMPERS HER — she digs ONE-HANDED, the dark-blue swaddled infant clutched to her chest in the other arm, unable to use both hands, the cruel difficulty of searching for one child while holding the other; she shields the baby as she works, the bundle shifting against her.
5. 6. LINE: the raw avalanche scar and the small patch of snow she claws at, the only disturbance in the immense white. SHAPE: her small huddled rounded dark form against the formless white waste. TONE: REVERSAL held — the small DARK grieving figure on the huge BRIGHT white, drowned in white, alone. COLOR: near-monochrome cold grey-white, her dark figure and the dark-blue bundle the only notes. MOVEMENT: her small frantic clawing against the vast stillness of the settled snow and the slow drift of powder and fog. CONTRAST & AFFINITY: the desolation after the peak — emptied, vast, lonely.

"Umai!.. UMAI!.."

She listens — nothing, only the wind and the hiss of settling snow — and she DIGS again, faster, more frantic, flinging snow, scrabbling deeper, the baby hampering her one arm, shielding the bundle as she tears at the snow. She calls again into the emptiness, lips on twos:

"Umai!.."

No answer. She keeps digging, keeps searching, tiny and alone in the endless white. Hold on her small figure clawing the vast snow, the white swallowing her voice. End.

DIRECTOR'S NOTES:
1. THE SCENE — full-gallop chase in the dusk blizzard, brutal and fast. We RIDE as RIDER 1 (first-person), chasing a sprinting wolf, leaning low and reaching down to seize it by the scruff in the manner of a kok-boru player — and the wolf twists and savages our arm. Then a second wolf hits from the blind side; we cut to an external view as he is torn from the saddle and the pack swarms him. Savage, dynamic, with REAL PHYSICS and a visible causal chain — every wound has its on-screen cause.
2. POV CRAFT (SHOTS 1–2, first-person) — we see THROUGH RIDER 1's eyes: at the bottom and sides of the frame, the horse's tossing mane, neck and withers (the horse from <<<image_4>>>) and our own gloved hands and chapan-sleeved forearms reaching forward out from under the camera; the wolf running ahead of us; the snowfield streaking toward and under us; blowing snow and spindrift flying INTO the lens. The camera IS his head — it bounces and pitches with the four-beat gallop, lurches as he leans, jolts with every stride, snow stinging the view, the world heaving — a living, breathing, violently handheld first-person, never gimbal-smooth, never locked. His hands/forearms (in chapan sleeves) are the only part of him we see. Do NOT show his face or body in the POV shots.
3. REAL PHYSICS AND CAUSALITY — the horse gallops with true four-beat weight (felt as the POV bounce); we lean low and our sleeved arm stretches DOWN and FORWARD for the wolf's scruff; the wolf is a heavy animal — when our hand seizes it, it twists its WHOLE body mid-stride and lunges BACK toward us, and its jaws clamp CRUSHING onto our forearm right at the lens — cause before effect; that twisting weight and the bite WRENCH the view sideways and down (we are dragged off balance); then a SECOND wolf launches from the blind side — and ON THAT IMPACT we CUT to the external SHOT 3, where RIDER 1 is slammed from the saddle, hits the snow HARD and TUMBLES with momentum, the riderless horse galloping on, and the pack swarms him. The slam is the cut point from POV to external.
4. BRUTALITY STAGED, NOT LINGERED — fast, hard, physical: the crushing bite at the lens, dark blood, the swarming pack. Savagery through motion, dark mass and sound, not slow anatomical detail.
5. CAMERA LAW (handheld / Lubezki, applied within each shot) — SHOTS 1–2: subjective first-person handheld, the camera as the rider's head, pitching and bouncing with the gallop, lurching with his lean, immersed in the storm with snow flying into the lens, natural dusk storm light only. SHOT 3: external AGGRESSIVE HANDHELD racing alongside, violently jolting, wind-whipped, horizon tilting and never level, a hard DUTCH TILT as he goes down, one continuous motivated move; never gimbal-smooth, never tripod-locked, never mechanical. Natural light only, palette from the scene.
6. COMPOSITION (SHOT 3 external — frame tells the story, by thirds, not centered) — LINE: the diagonal of the chase and the fall as the line of dynamics; on the fall a reeling dutch tilt. SHAPE: the dark angular lunging wolves converging on the falling man. TONE: dark masses (rider, horse, wolves) against the pale storm-lit snow, the figure the focal point until the dark pack mass engulfs him; the pack TRAPS and frames him. BIG VS SMALL: the lone man swallowed by the converging dark pack and the vast storm. Off-center, never dead-centered.
7. SECONDARY ACTION on twos — in POV, the horse's mane and our chapan sleeves whipping with follow-through, breath-vapor tearing past the lens; in the external shot, RIDER 1's chapan skirts and fur hat whipping, the horse's mane and tail streaming, the wolves' fur rippling, harness swinging, breath-vapor of horse and man torn off in the wind, snow bursting from hooves and impacts as drawn powder on twos.
8. LIGHT — deep dusk in a blizzard, dim cold blue-grey storm light, soft, no sun, NO rays, NO beams, NO god rays, NO volumetric shafts, the figures dark masses against the pale snow. CORRECT NEUTRAL WHITE BALANCE, NOT a blue filter, muted desaturated; the blood a dark muted red, stark on the snow but never glossy, never bright.

THE SCENE — the turning point: ANA pushes out through the yurt's door-flap and walks out to the two old men, and against the cold old man who would abandon her child she declares they must find her daughter — she is out there — and then she turns and walks away alone, breaking from the tribe to search. A scene of FACES, of one woman against the cold old man and the tribe, and of a lone figure walking into the cold. Played slow and grave, the emotion in held looks and posture.
2. ACTING — THE HEART OF THE SCENE, faces must ACT in stepped held poses on twos, each beat given TIME: ANA — grief mastered into iron resolve as she emerges, her face set and certain, eyes still red and wet but steady and unshakeable, jaw firm; not hysterical — a quiet, immovable conviction, and a defiant fire toward the cold old man; on the line about her daughter, a flicker of pain crosses but the resolve holds. DIRECTOR'S NOTES:
1. THE SCENE — a tense confrontation at dusk beside the yurt, the dark turning point. A COLD HARD OLD MAN presses the AKSAKAL to abandon the search — they will not search anymore, the camp will not die for one child, they move on NOW; he has ill intent. The AKSAKAL resists, grieved and cornered. Inside, ANA hears every cold word. A scene of FACES, PAUSES and the CAMERA telling the power: the cold man towers, the elder is pressed down, the mother is trapped.
2. CAMERA DIRECTS THE POWER — camera HEIGHT and MOVEMENT carry the story, not just coverage:
   - The COLD OLD MAN is shot from a LOW ANGLE looking UP at him — he TOWERS, dominant, a looming threat; and the camera slowly PUSHES IN on him as he presses, tightening the menace.
   - The AKSAKAL is shot from a SLIGHT HIGH ANGLE looking DOWN at him — pressed down, cornered, the burden bending him, losing ground; not grand, but weighed and small under the pressure.
   - ANA inside is shot LOW and TIGHT, the dark felt walls crowding the frame around her — trapped, boxed in, the claustrophobia of overhearing her child being given up, the walls closing on her.
   This height contrast — looming antagonist vs pressed-down elder vs boxed-in mother — IS the drama.
3. ACTING — faces must ACT in stepped held poses on twos, each beat given TIME. The COLD OLD MAN — cold, hard, stubborn, ill-intentioned, a flinty unyielding stare, a hard chopping gesture, leaning in with pressure, no warmth, he wants the child abandoned and does not hide it. The AKSAKAL — resisting, his lined face heavy with grief and refusal, jaw tightening, a pained shake of the head, cornered by the hard man's logic, the burden crushing him. ANA (inside) — flinch, then horror and anguish as she hears leave her daughter, eyes welling, brow wrenching, then anger and a HARDENING, resolve being born against the cold man. Faces clearly lit and legible, never blank.
4. COMPOSITION — CONFLICT and SEPARATION: the two old men as opposing masses, the cold man pressing IN and dominant, the AKSAKAL holding ground and pressed; the felt WALL of the yurt the border between the men outside and ANA inside, framed between them, ANA pressed against the inner wall. By thirds, never centered, the dark wall and cold space the negative space of the gulf opening between ANA and the tribe.
5. FRAMED INK STAGING — masses: the cold antagonist's angular hard shape looming, the AKSAKAL's shape weighed and bending, against pale snow and dim sky; inside, ANA a dark grieving shape boxed by dark felt, lit low and warm by ember-glow.
6. CAMERA CRAFT — living HANDHELD, breathing, never gimbal-smooth or locked, never mechanical; the slow PUSH IN on the antagonist and the held pressed framing on the elder are motivated and human, the camera breathing with the tension. Natural light only.
7. SECONDARY ACTION on twos — the two old men's white beards and chapans stirring in the cold wind with follow-through, breath-vapor torn off, ANA's kimeshek ends and the dark-blue bundle shifting; smoke, ember-glow and drifting snow smooth.
8. LIGHT — cold blue dusk outside, warm low ember/firelight inside, soft, no sun, NO rays, NO beams, NO god rays, faces clearly lit and readable never black voids. Correct neutral white balance, NOT a blue filter, muted desaturated; the warm interior glow low and soft, not a beam on faces.

DIRECTOR'S NOTES:
1. THE SCENE — night at the winter camp, a fire burning, the tribe gathered before the COLD OLD MAN. He gives a rousing, ruthless speech: the wolves are slaughtering the herds, so they will hunt and kill the wolves themselves — and he announces a BOUNTY: for every wolf killed, a head of livestock from his own herd; whoever brings the most, gets the most. The crowd catches fire. A demagogue at the fire bending a whole people to his will — and one old man, the AKSAKAL, the single soul who will not be swept up.
2. COMPOSITION TELLS THE STORY — ONE MASTERS THE MANY: the visual story is a lone man taking command of a crowd, the scattered people fusing into a single swayed mass under his raised hand.
 - The COLD OLD MAN raised ABOVE the crowd, shot from a LOW ANGLE looking UP — he dominates, grows, owns the frame; firelight from below makes him the demagogue, a hard idol against the night.
 - The CROWD begins as separate dark figures and, as the speech builds, FUSES into one dark surging mass — a forest of raised arms moving as one organism, the unity of a crowd seized; they fill the lower frame, bound by the fire.
 - The FIRE the bright binding center, the hot core the mass gathers around, its glow the only warmth in the cold night.
 - The AKSAKAL the single CRACK in the unity — one still figure against the surge, a point of attention through contrast, the conscience that will not move.
 By thirds, never centered. The frame says: the idol above, the mass fused below, one crack of refusal within it.
3. CAMERA LAW (LUBEZKI handheld craft, with HANDHELD) — every shot ONE continuous motivated handheld move, never static, never locked, never gimbal-smooth, never mechanical:
 - HANDHELD LIVING PRESENCE — the camera is held in human hands, a living breathing presence DOWN IN the crowd among the people, a soft organic sway and drift, jolts, jostled by the gathering, alive; it breathes harder as the crowd's energy rises.
 - CONTINUOUS MOTIVATED MOVEMENT — each shot one fluid motivated move driven by the speech: a slow relentless PUSH IN on the old man as he builds, a sweep through the surging mass on the roar, a turn to find the still AKSAKAL — not fixed frames.
 - IMMERSED IN THE ELEMENT — the camera INSIDE the night and the gathering: sparks and smoke drift across the lens, breath-vapor and firelight haze in the frame, we are in the crowd, not observing it.
 - WIDE IMMERSIVE FRAMING — close, enveloping framing that puts us bodily among the people, the fire and the looming old man wrapping around us.
 - NATURAL LIGHT ONLY — lit solely by the fire and the cold night, no artificial light, no rays, no beams.
 - PALETTE FROM THE SCENE — the warm fire-orange and cold night-blue, the whole palette drawn from the fire and the dark.
4. ACTING — THE EMOTION, faces must ACT in stepped held poses on twos, each beat given TIME, faces lit by firelight and legible, never blank:
 - The COLD OLD MAN — commanding, ruthless, a hard charismatic fire; jaw set, eyes glinting cold and certain, sweeping authoritative gestures, his arm THRUST UP on the bounty and the call, feeding on the crowd's response, a thin hard satisfaction as they catch — power, no warmth beneath it.
 - The CROWD (front faces readable) — moving from wary listening, to widening eyes and leaning in at the bounty, to greed and bloodlust and resolve, mouths opening in shouts, fists punching up, faces lit and hungry, swept into the hunt as one.
 - The AKSAKAL — NOT joining; his lined old face grave and troubled, brows drawn, mouth tight, his eyes lowering and turning from the fire in quiet sorrow and disquiet, the one face set against the fervor, grieved by what this unleashes.
5. FRAMED INK STAGING — read as masses: the COLD OLD MAN a dark commanding upright shape raised against night and firelight, the CROWD a dark clustered fusing mass around the bright fire, the AKSAKAL a single still dark shape breaking the surge. CONCEAL: night and smoke half-veil the deeper crowd, hiding the count, the mass swelling beyond the dark. CAMERA HEIGHT: LOW up at the dominant old man (his power); down in the mass of the crowd; level on the still AKSAKAL.
6. SECONDARY ACTION on twos — the old man's beard and chapan and thrust-up sleeve whipping with follow-through, the crowd's clothing and many breath-vapors, the AKSAKAL's beard and chapan, sparks and smoke streaming off the fire, breath-vapor of all torn off in the cold; fire-flicker, sparks, smoke and drifting snow smooth.
7. LIGHT — cold blue night, warm firelight from BELOW on the old man and the crowd's front faces, soft, no rays NO beams NO god rays, faces clearly lit and readable never black voids. Correct neutral white balance, NOT a blue filter on the cold, the firelight warm and flickering but not a beam; muted desaturated.

«Аттарға мініңдер! Ертең аңға шығамыз!»

COMPOSITION (the crack in the unity): amid the roaring fused crowd and the leaping fire, the AKSAKAL (<<<image_2>>>) a single STILL dark figure, off-center, the surging mass and raised arms around him as he stands unmoving — the one point of stillness in the fervor, the conscience apart. His lined face grave and troubled on twos, brows drawn, mouth tight, his eyes lowering and turning from the fire in sorrow and disquiet at what has been unleashed. Hold on his still grieved face against the roaring crowd. End.
